The DPDP (Removal of Difficulties) Order, 2026 Two small textual changes to the DPDP Act. What changed, what didn't, and what to update now. Section 9 · Children & PwD Section 10 · SDF audits Compliance checklist Adv. Ashwani Kumar · Advocate | Data Privacy & Technology Law 01 / 07

THE BASICS What is this Order? ISSUED BY POWER USED MeitY Section 43(1) Central Government DPDP Act, 2023 — removal of difficulties ISSUED NATURE 5 Oct 2026 Textual fixes Published in the Gazette on 7 Clarifies wording; creates no Oct 2026 new obligations PROVISIONS TOUCHED Section 9(1) and Section 10(2)(c)(ii) Children's / PwD data, and Significant Data Fiduciary audits Adv. Ashwani Kumar 02 / 07

CHANGE 1 · SECTION 9(1) Children and persons with disability BEFORE “…personal data of a child or a person with disability…” AFTER “…personal data of a child or of a person with disability…” The two categories now read as parallel, independent classes. Verifiable consent of the parent (for a child) or the lawful guardian (for a person with disability) is required, exactly as before. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 03 / 07

CHANGE 2 · SECTION 10(2)(C)(II) Significant Data Fiduciary audits BEFORE “periodic audit” AFTER “periodic data audit” The SDF audit is about data protection and processing compliance, not a general financial or operational audit. Scope, auditor engagement and audit records should say so. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 04 / 07

No new duties. Same stakes. 1 Verifiable parental / guardian consent before processing a child's or a person with disability's data. 2 No tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising directed at children. 3 SDF duties: Data Protection Officer in India, independent data auditor, periodic DPIA. Breach of children's data obligations: up to ₹200 crore. Breach of SDF obligations: up to ₹150 crore. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 05 / 07
